verdict.rationale: Proa documents streaming server-rendered HTML in two modes: flushing in document order, or letting Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order so slow data does not block the page. Its islands architecture sends server-rendered HTML first, with only small per-island JS modules on a ~1.3 KB gzipped runtime, which supports faster perceived loads before client code arrives. Missing for 10: in-depth API docs for the streaming/Suspense mechanism (the evidence is short homepage claims) and independent or hands-on corroboration of streaming behavior and perceived-load gains.
